annotation_description: Casting Kaito before combat is suboptimal. Preacher of the Schism is about to attack, and if the opponent is at the highest life or tied, it creates a vampire token. More importantly, if Kimi25 Spike has the most life (18 vs 16), Preacher draws a card on attack. By casting Kaito pre-combat, they miss the opportunity to use Kaito's Ninjutsu ability — if Preacher attacks and is unblocked (opponent has no creatures), they could return Preacher to hand and put Kaito onto the battlefield tapped and attacking via Ninjutsu for {1}{U}{B}, saving 1 mana. Additionally, Kaito attacking as a 3/4 would deal combat damage, and then using his 0 ability would draw a card since the opponent lost life this turn. They also lose the Preacher attack trigger (draw + vampire token). However, casting Kaito normally and then attacking with both Kaito (as a 3/4 creature during your turn) and Preacher could also be strong. But the Ninjutsu line is strictly better: pay 3 mana for Kaito via Ninjutsu, Kaito deals combat damage, use 0 ability to surveil 2 and draw 1 (opponent lost life), then replay Preacher post-combat or next turn. The Ninjutsu line saves mana and generates card advantage, while pre-combat Kaito means he can still attack but you don't get the surprise ninjutsu value and you telegraph to the opponent.

Kaito is a 3/4 hexproof creature during Kimi25's turn, and the opponent has no creatures and no untapped mana. Attacking with only Preacher leaves 3 damage on the table for no reason. Additionally, if Kaito dealt combat damage, the 0 loyalty ability would draw a card since the opponent lost life this turn.

Played a second Soulstone Sanctuary (colorless-only land with a weak creature-land activation) over Restless Reef, which enters tapped but provides colored mana and is a significantly better creature-land (4/4 deathtouch vs 3/3 vigilance). Since this is postcombat main, the tapped entry of Restless Reef doesn't matter. Having two colorless lands constrains colored mana for cards like Bitter Triumph, Deep-Cavern Bat, and Flitterwing Nuisance in hand.

Failed to activate Kaito's 0 loyalty ability in postcombat main. Since the opponent lost life this turn (from Kaito's combat damage), the 0 ability would have provided Surveil 2 AND drawn a card, all at zero loyalty cost. This is pure free card advantage that was left on the table.

DSV3 Proud is casting Superior Spider-Man as a copy of a creature card in a graveyard. They chose Preacher of the Schism (a 2/4 deathtouch with conditional card draw and token creation) over Overlord of the Balemurk (a 5/5 that mills 4 and returns a creature/planeswalker from graveyard to hand on ETB and attack). As a 4/4 base copy, either way the stats are 4/4. However, Overlord of the Balemurk's ETB would immediately mill 4 cards and return a creature or planeswalker from graveyard to hand - this could recover the other Superior Spider-Man or generate significant value. Additionally, Overlord triggers on every attack, providing recurring card advantage through mill and recursion. Preacher of the Schism's abilities are conditional on life totals (DSV3 Proud is at 12 life vs opponent's 16, so they're not tied or highest - meaning no card draw trigger and no vampire token). The Preacher's deathtouch is nice but the Overlord provides far more value in this position.

Flitterwing Nuisance has its -1/-1 counter available to remove. Activating its ability ({2}{U}, remove a counter) before combat damage would draw a card for each creature dealing combat damage to a player this turn. With both Deep-Cavern Bat and Flitterwing unblocked, this would draw 2 cards and also make Flitterwing a 2/2 (dealing 1 extra damage). Drawing 2 cards for 3 mana is excellent value.

Declined to activate Flitterwing Nuisance's ability to remove its -1/-1 counter before combat. With opponent's only creature (Superior Spider-Man) tapped, both Deep-Cavern Bat and Flitterwing Nuisance would deal combat damage unblocked, drawing 2 cards. Additionally, removing the counter makes Flitterwing a 2/2 instead of 1/1, dealing 1 extra damage. This is significant card advantage missed.

Playing Restless Reef (enters tapped) instead of an untapped land like Island or Gloomlake Verge costs 1 mana this turn cycle. With Bitter Triumph and Requiting Hex in hand as removal options, having maximum mana available for instant-speed interaction against the opponent's 5/5 Superior Spider-Man is important. An untapped land would leave 4 mana up after casting Deep-Cavern Bat instead of 3.

Kimi25 Spike cast Deep-Cavern Bat without first playing a land from hand. They have Island and Gloomlake Verge available. Playing a land first is free and would leave more mana open for interaction (e.g., Bitter Triumph with 1B up, or Requiting Hex).

Casting Floodpits Drowner (a flash creature) in precombat main phase rather than holding it. While it puts a stun counter on the tapped Superior Spider-Man either way, casting it now uses 2 mana that could be held for Bitter Triumph or other responses. Flash creatures should generally be deployed as late as possible to maintain flexibility and information advantage.

message: Select a creature an opponent controls
annotation_description: Floodpits Drowner's ETB taps a creature and puts a stun counter on it. Superior Spider-Man is a 4/4 (copied Deep-Cavern Bat but as a 4/4) that is already tapped, but putting a stun counter on it would keep it tapped through DSV3 Proud's next untap step, effectively time-walking their biggest threat. The Vampire Token is just a 1/1 token that poses minimal threat. By tapping the Vampire Token instead of stunning Superior Spider-Man, Kimi25 Spike wastes the Drowner's powerful stun effect on an irrelevant creature while leaving the opponent's main threat free to untap and attack/block next turn. Additionally, Floodpits Drowner has the activated ability to shuffle itself and a creature with a stun counter into their owners' libraries — stunning Superior Spider-Man would have enabled permanently removing it.

Kimi25 Spike had exactly {2}{U} available from untapped lands (Gloomlake Verge, Soulstone Sanctuary, Restless Reef) to activate Flitterwing Nuisance's ability (remove the -1/-1 counter to draw a card for each creature dealing combat damage this turn). With 3 unblocked creatures, this would have drawn 3 cards — a massive card advantage opportunity missed for free, as the counter removal also makes Flitterwing a 2/2 for more damage.

Flitterwing Nuisance has a -1/-1 counter that can be removed for {2}{U} to draw a card whenever a creature deals combat damage this turn. With opponent's only creature tapped and unable to block, this would draw at least 1-2 cards AND make the Nuisance a 2/2 instead of 1/1, dealing an extra point of damage to the opponent at 7 life. Kimi25 Spike had exactly {2}{U} available from untapped lands (Gloomlake Verge, Soulstone Sanctuary, Restless Reef).

Additionally, tapping Cavern now means it's unavailable later in the turn for casting Formidable Speaker (in hand), where Cavern's colored mana ability could actually be useful.

Deep-Cavern Bat is currently exiling DSV3 Proud's Bitter Triumph. Destroying the bat would return Bitter Triumph to hand - a premium removal spell that DSV3 Proud desperately needs at 7 life. Instead, DSV3 Proud chose to destroy Floodpits Drowner, a utility creature, missing the opportunity to recover their best removal spell.

Opponent is at 6 life with their only creature (Superior Spider-Man) tapped. Activating Restless Reef for 2UB (using Soulstone Sanctuary + Soulstone Sanctuary + Gloomlake Verge + Swamp) makes it a 4/4 deathtouch attacker. Combined with Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1 flying) and Flitterwing Nuisance (1/1 flying), that's exactly 6 damage for lethal with no available blockers.

Requiting Hex can only destroy a creature with mana value 2 or less. The opponent's only creature is Superior Spider-Man (MV 4), which is not a legal target. The player would either need to target their own creature (terrible) or the spell fizzles. Meanwhile, Bitter Triumph in hand could destroy Superior Spider-Man, and they should also play a land first (Island or Gloomlake Verge) since they haven't played one this turn.

Targeted a 1/1 Vampire Token with Bitter Triumph instead of the 4/4 Superior Spider-Man. Superior Spider-Man is currently tapped but will untap and be a significant blocker next turn, while a Vampire Token is a minimal threat. At 6 life, the opponent needs to block effectively and Superior Spider-Man is their best blocker.

Missed a free land drop with two lands in hand (Gloomlake Verge and Island). Playing an additional land provides more mana next turn for activating Restless Reef ({2}{U}{B}) or casting future draws, with no downside.

Bringer of the Last Gift is likely the game-winning play here. It wipes the opponent's board (Deep-Cavern Bat, Flitterwing Nuisance), then DSV3 gets back Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5), Spider-Man, and Deceit from graveyard plus keeps Bringer (6/6 flying), creating an overwhelming board. Opponent only gets back Kaito and Floodpits Drowner. At 7 life facing that board, the game is essentially over.

Kimi25 Spike attacked with only the two Deep-Cavern Bats for 2 damage when they could have also activated Restless Reef ({2}{U}{B}) to make it a 4/4 deathtouch attacker with no blockers available (Superior Spider-Man is tapped). This would deal 6 total damage (8→2) instead of 2 (8→6), putting the opponent in critical range.

Declined to activate Restless Reef as a 4/4 attacker, missing 4 extra damage (plus mill 4 trigger). This would have put the opponent from 8 to 2 life instead of 6, significantly increasing pressure. The opponent's Superior Spider-Man is tapped so there are no blockers. Keeping mana open for Tragic Trajectory is less valuable since -2/-2 doesn't kill the 4/4 Spider-Man without the void condition being met.
